newsitem.title: UK: Growth factor enriches cancer patient blood-study.
newsitem.headline: Growth factor enriches cancer patient blood-study.

text.p: A newly-discovered growth-enhancing chemical can enrich the blood of cancer patients and help them better tolerate chemotherapy, Australian researchers said on Friday.
Dr Russell Basser of the Royal Melbourne Hospital in Victoria, working with California-based biotechnology firm Amgen Inc, found the chemical increased the blood platelet count of the patients.
Blood platelets are important for making the blood clot. Chemotherapy for cancer can reduce the number of platelets, making patients prone to dangerous bleeding.
The growth factor is a cytokine, a chemical used by cells to signal one another. It is known variously as thrombopoietin, Mpl-ligand or megakaryocyte growth and development factor.
Basser's group grew an artificial version of the cytokine in bacteria and gave it to 13 patients with advanced cancer. Four others got a placebo.
They found the growth factor caused platelet counts to increase, and the more the volunteers were given, the more platelets they had. There were no major side-effects.
"There were no substantial alterations in performance status, body temperature, vital signs or body weight during the study," the researchers wrote in the Lancet medical journal.
They said the chemical was likely to be useful for treating chemotherapy patients.
